newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Centrica cuts gas prices in SW England.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Centrica cuts gas prices in SW England.

text.p: Centrica Plc, the gas supply arm demerged from British Gas last month, on Tuesday launched a scheme which offers customers in south-west England discounts of up to 12 percent on their bills.

But industry regulator Ofgas still has to decide whether it will give the green light to the so-called ValuePlus price discount. Centrica will be forced to withdraw the scheme if Ofgas decides competition in the area has not been fully established yet.
The south west was the first region in Britain where competition was introduced in the domestic gas market after it was opened up in April 1996. Nation-wide competition is envisaged by 1998.
Centrica said it had launched its new ValuePlus scheme to fight off the aggressive marketing of competing suppliers.

Rivals such as major oil and gas companies and electricity firms have moved into the southwest, undercutting Centrica prices by up to 20 percent and luring away about 20 percent of the former monopoly's customers.

ValuePlus is available to customers who choose to pay by monthly direct debit and are prepared to stay with Centrica, which still markets its products under the British Gas brand name, for a minimum 12 months.

"We're committed to offering a value for money package of price and service which will make customers choose to stay with us," said Mike Alexander, managing director of Centrica's domestic trading business said.
But Ofgas said it will consult the views of other gas suppliers and the Gas Consumer Council on Centrica's move. The consultation period can last up to 28 days.
The Gas Consumers Council said it sympathised with Centrica, but added the price cut of up to 12 percent could be judged as premature.
